newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF considers dropping tax rule on Euroyen bonds.
newsitem.headline: MOF considers dropping tax rule on Euroyen bonds.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance said on Tuesday it may scrap a rule which exempts a withholding tax on income gains from Euroyen bond investments.
The tax rule was originally intended to stimulate Euroyen purchases by non-Japanese residents, but Japanese investors have become the main Euroyen buyers, a ministry official said.
"There is a need to review this rule. At this point, we do not see much need to keep such a rule," the official said.
"But nothing is final until around the end of year when the government decides on its budget plan."

The official said the ministry intends to abolish the tax exemption rule by April 1998, when it is also expected to abolish the current 40-day lock-up rule on domestic sales of Euroyen bonds issued by Japanese borrowers.
